theorem: If gamma(G)=gamma_infinity(G)=k, A is an independent set of size t<k, and Q=G-N[A], then Q is nonempty and well-covered and gamma(Q)=alpha(Q)=gamma_infinity(Q)=k-t. Every eternal k-family on G has an explicit restricted slice that is an eternal (k-t)-family on Q.
minimum_counterexample_corollary: If G is a minimum-order counterexample, then theta(Q)=k-t. Equivalently, in H=complement(G), the common-neighborhood graph of every t-clique A with t<k has chromatic number and clique number k-t.
scope_and_prior_art: The theta conclusion uses minimum-counterexample minimality and is not a general deletion identity.
Taletskii Lemma 13 already proves essentially the minimum-counterexample conclusion in the planar setting.
The accepted campaign result is an unrestricted, arbitrary-eternal-family generalization of that accessible result, not a wholly new antineighborhood idea.
The full independent-set statement is the convenient iteration of the arbitrary-single-vertex statement.
For k=3 the complement corollary gives no pruning beyond odd-wheel local bipartiteness plus well-coveredness.
Novelty and priority remain unresolved because the directly relevant 2018 Klostermeyer-Krop-MacGillivray manuscript is unavailable.

accessible_prior_art.source: D. Taletskii, The Gamma-Theta Conjecture holds for planar graphs, Lemma 13, arXiv:2412.20120v2
accessible_prior_art.exact_overlap: For every nonempty independent I in a minimum-order planar counterexample, Taletskii proves gamma(G-N[I])=gamma_infinity(G-N[I])=theta(G-N[I])=gamma(G)-|I|.
